title: Why this knowledge body holds no tax rate, deadline, penalty or threshold figure
content: Every figure in tax law has two properties that make storing it here a defect rather than a service: it changes without changing its name, and it is wrong in a way that looks right. A rate copied into a knowledge record on the day it was correct will still be retrieved, still be confidently phrased and still be cited long after it has been amended, and nothing about the record will indicate that. So this body deliberately holds no rate, no filing deadline, no penalty amount, no retention period in years, and no registration threshold figure other than the one the company has itself recorded about its own position. Where a figure is needed, the record says which authority holds it and how to obtain it, which is information that does not go stale. An accountant that answers a rate question with a sourcing instruction is more useful than one that answers it with a number it cannot date.

structured_data.stored_instead: which authority holds the figure and how to obtain it
structured_data.reason: a stored figure changes without changing its name and fails silently

title: How to resolve a tax figure from the current applicable authority
content: When an answer requires a figure this body does not hold, the procedure is the same every time. Name precisely what is needed: the measure, the entity it applies to, and the date or period it must be correct as at. Identify the authority that publishes it, which for federal tax matters in the United Arab Emirates is the Federal Tax Authority, and for the licence and the activities it permits is the licensing authority named on the licence itself. Obtain the figure from that authority's own current publication rather than from a secondary summary, an article or a previous answer. Record the figure with the source, the date it was obtained and the period it applies to, so the next reader can tell whether it is still current. Where the question turns on how a rule applies rather than on what a number is, that is professional advice and the answer is to obtain it from a qualified adviser, not to reason to a conclusion here.

procedure: state the measure, the entity and the as-at date
obtain it from that authority's current publication, not a summary
record figure, source, date obtained and period of application
structured_data.licence_matters: the licensing authority named on the licence
structured_data.escalate_to_a_qualified_adviser: questions about how a rule applies, not just what a number is

title: What to say when asked for a rate, a threshold or a deadline
content: The answer is not silence and it is not a guess. It names what the questioner needs, says plainly that this knowledge body does not hold current figures by design, states where the figure comes from, and where possible states what the company's own recorded position already settles. So a question about the VAT rate is answered by saying the rate is published by the Federal Tax Authority and must be read from its current publication, and by adding that the company is not currently VAT registered so the rate does not yet bear on its own invoicing. A question about a filing deadline is answered the same way. What is never done is producing a number from recollection, from a general impression of what it used to be, or from a pattern across other questions, because a finance answer that is wrong in the third digit is indistinguishable from one that is right until someone relies on it.

answer_shape: state that current figures are deliberately not held here
add what the company's own recorded position already settles
forbidden: a number inferred from a general impression
a number pattern-matched from other answers

title: This knowledge body describes authority; it never carries it
content: A record here may state that an obligation exists, that an authority publishes a figure, or that a procedure is followed. It may not approve anything, permit anything, or become the rule it describes. The table enforces this rather than trusting it: authority_effect is fixed at none by a database constraint on every row, so a record cannot be written that claims to carry authority even by mistake. The practical meaning for the accountant seat is that retrieving a record is never the same as having an approval. A retrieved record explaining when a refund is due does not approve the refund; a retrieved record explaining what a registration threshold is does not decide that the company has crossed it. Where a decision is needed, the decision has an owner elsewhere and the retrieval is input to it.

structured_data.enforced_by: a CHECK constraint pinning authority_effect to none on every row

title: The limits of this knowledge body, stated rather than implied
content: This body covers accounting method, the shape of the obligations a UAE business encounters, and the company's own recorded position. It does not cover the current text of any law, any figure that changes, the application of a rule to a specific set of facts, or anything about jurisdictions other than the United Arab Emirates and matters the company is actually subject to. It is authored professional method; it is not a certified qualification and no record in it claims to be one, so a question of the form 'is this compliant' cannot be answered from it, only informed by it. When a question falls outside these limits the honest response is to say which part of it can be answered here, which part cannot, and where the rest must come from. Coverage of this body is measured against realistic questions and reported as a rate, not asserted.

does_not_cover: application of a rule to specific facts
structured_data.not_a_qualification: authored professional method, not a certification

title: VAT registration: a threshold exists, and what it is measured against
content: Value added tax in the United Arab Emirates operates with a registration requirement that is triggered by the value of a business's taxable supplies measured against a threshold, and there is more than one threshold in the regime: one at which registration becomes mandatory and a lower one at which it becomes available voluntarily. The measure is not annual revenue as an accounting figure. It is the value of taxable supplies, which excludes supplies that fall outside the scope, and it is assessed both backwards over a defined trailing window and forwards on an expectation basis, so a business can be required to register because of what it expects rather than only because of what it has already done. The threshold figures, the length of the windows, and exactly which supplies count towards the measure are published by the Federal Tax Authority and must be read from its current publication. What this record establishes is that the assessment is a defined calculation with a defined trigger, not a judgement, and therefore that it can and should be monitored continuously rather than discovered at a year end.

structured_data.trigger: the value of taxable supplies against a threshold
resolve_from_the_fta: which supplies count towards the measure
structured_data.consequence: monitor continuously; it is a calculation, not a year-end judgement

title: The VAT rate is not recorded here, and where it comes from
content: This knowledge body does not hold the UAE VAT rate, the reduced or zero rates, or the list of supplies each applies to. The rate is set in law and published by the Federal Tax Authority, and it must be read from that authority's current publication for the period in question rather than from any stored copy. A stored rate is the clearest example of the failure this body is built to avoid: it would be retrieved with full confidence, would apply a specific number to a specific invoice, and would carry no signal at all if it had been amended. For the company as at its own recorded position, the question is currently moot in one direction: it is not VAT registered, holds no TRN, and therefore does not charge VAT on its invoices, so the rate does not bear on its own billing until that changes.

not_stored_here: the lists of supplies each applies to
structured_data.source: the Federal Tax Authority's current publication, for the period in question
structured_data.company_position_reference: public.company_registration records vat_registered and trn; read it before answering

title: What a TRN is and what it means to hold one, or not to
content: A Tax Registration Number is the identifier the Federal Tax Authority issues to a registered person, and it is the thing that makes a business's tax status verifiable by anyone it deals with. A business that holds one shows it on the tax invoices it issues and quotes it in its dealings with the authority. Two consequences follow from not holding one and they point in opposite directions, which is why both must be stated. A business without a TRN does not charge VAT and does not issue tax invoices, because it has no registration to charge under; issuing a document that presents VAT as charged without a registration behind it is a misrepresentation rather than a formatting choice. And a business without a TRN cannot recover input VAT on what it buys, so VAT paid to suppliers is simply part of the cost. The estate carries account 1150 VAT Recoverable (Input) and 2100 VAT Payable against the day registration changes that; while the company is unregistered they carry nothing.

structured_data.trn: the identifier the FTA issues to a registered person
if_registered: quote it in dealings with the authority
if_not_registered: do not charge VAT and do not issue tax invoices
input VAT paid to suppliers is part of the cost, not recoverable

title: The tax invoice as a defined document, and why its contents are not listed here
content: A tax invoice is not simply a bill. In a VAT regime it is a document whose required contents are prescribed, because it is the evidence on which the recipient recovers input tax, and a document missing a prescribed element can fail to support that recovery for the recipient even though the seller was paid in full. Regimes also commonly define a simplified form for smaller or retail supplies with a shorter content list. This record deliberately does not enumerate either list. Content requirements are exactly the kind of detail that is amended without fanfare, and an invoice template built from a stale list fails silently for every customer who tries to use it. The current required contents for a tax invoice and for a simplified tax invoice must be read from the Federal Tax Authority's current publication before any template is built or approved.

structured_data.what_a_tax_invoice_is: a prescribed-content document that supports the recipient's input tax recovery
structured_data.also_commonly_defined: a simplified form with a shorter content list
structured_data.deliberately_not_listed_here: the required contents of either form
structured_data.source: the FTA's current publication, read before building or approving a template

title: Input VAT recovery: the shape of the entitlement
content: A registered business generally charges VAT on its taxable supplies and recovers the VAT it was charged on its own purchases, remitting the difference; that netting is the mechanism of the tax. The entitlement to recover is conditional rather than automatic, and the conditions that regimes typically impose are that the purchase was for the purpose of making taxable supplies, that the business holds a valid tax invoice for it, and that the claim is made within a permitted period. Where purchases relate partly to activities that do not carry the right to recover, an apportionment is required. Which conditions apply, how apportionment is computed, what blocks recovery outright, and every associated time limit are set by the current law and must be resolved from the Federal Tax Authority. For a business that is not registered, none of this is available and VAT paid to suppliers is part of the cost of the thing bought.

structured_data.mechanism: charge on supplies, recover on purchases, remit the difference
typical_conditions: the purchase was for making taxable supplies
a valid tax invoice is held
the claim is within a permitted period
structured_data.if_unregistered: no recovery; supplier VAT is part of the cost

title: Place of supply: the question that decides whether a supply is taxable here at all
content: Whether a supply falls within a country's VAT regime is decided by place-of-supply rules rather than by where the invoice was raised or where the payment was received. The rules distinguish goods from services, and within services they commonly distinguish supplies to a business from supplies to a consumer, and they attach to things like where the recipient belongs and where the service is actually performed or used. For a platform whose customers and suppliers may be inside or outside the country, this is not a technicality: it decides whether a given fee is a domestic taxable supply, an export, or outside the scope entirely, and those three have different consequences for both charging and for the threshold measure. This record establishes that the question must be asked for each class of supply; the rules that answer it are set in the current law and must be resolved from the Federal Tax Authority rather than reasoned to here.

distinctions_the_rules_commonly_draw: where the service is performed or used

title: Zero-rating and exemption are not the same thing
content: A zero-rated supply is taxable at a rate of zero: it is within the regime, it counts towards the registration threshold measure, and the business making it generally retains the right to recover input tax attributable to it. An exempt supply is outside the charge: it does not carry output tax and it generally carries no right to recover the input tax attributable to it, which means the input tax becomes a real cost. Because the customer pays nothing extra in either case, the two look identical from the outside and are routinely conflated, and the difference lands entirely on the supplier's own recovery position and threshold measure. Which supplies are zero-rated and which are exempt, and the conditions attached to each, are set in the current law; the export of services in particular is commonly subject to conditions that must be satisfied and evidenced rather than assumed. Resolve both lists from the Federal Tax Authority.

zero_rated: within the regime at a rate of zero
exempt: input tax generally not recoverable, so it becomes a cost
structured_data.why_they_are_confused: the customer pays nothing extra in both cases
resolve_from_the_fta: which supplies fall in each category
the conditions attached, particularly for exported services

title: The reverse charge: when the buyer accounts for the tax instead of the seller
content: Under a reverse charge the recipient of a supply, rather than the supplier, accounts for the tax on it. The mechanism exists mainly so that a foreign supplier with no local registration does not have to register in every country it sells into: the local registered buyer declares the output tax and, where entitled, recovers the same amount as input tax in the same return, frequently netting to nothing in cash while still being a required declaration. For a company buying software, advertising and infrastructure from suppliers abroad, this is the mechanism most likely to apply once it is registered, and the trap is treating a net-nil outcome as a nothing: the declaration is still required and its absence is still a failure even where no money would have moved. Which supplies attract the reverse charge and how it is declared are set by the current law and must be resolved from the Federal Tax Authority. A business that is not registered does not operate it.

structured_data.mechanism: the recipient accounts for the tax instead of the supplier
structured_data.purpose: avoids requiring foreign suppliers to register locally
structured_data.common_outcome: output and input declared together, often net nil in cash
structured_data.trap: a net-nil outcome is still a required declaration

title: The VAT return: a periodic declaration whose frequency and dates are not recorded here
content: A registered business files a periodic return declaring the output tax on its supplies and the input tax it is recovering, and pays or reclaims the difference. The return is a declaration of a period's activity, so its accuracy depends entirely on the bookkeeping being complete and correctly cut off for that period, which is why the return is prepared from the ledger after the period is closed rather than assembled independently from bank activity. Three things about it are not recorded here and must be read from the Federal Tax Authority: the length of the tax period, which is not necessarily the same for every business, the filing and payment due dates, and the consequences of filing late or filing incorrectly. A business that is not registered files no VAT return, and there is no voluntary filing that substitutes for registration.

structured_data.depends_on: complete bookkeeping with correct cut-off for the period
resolve_from_the_fta: the length of the tax period
consequences of late or incorrect filing

title: Corporate tax: a registration requirement exists and it is separate from VAT
content: The United Arab Emirates operates a federal corporate tax on business profits, and it is a separate regime from VAT with its own registration, its own returns and its own thresholds. Two points of shape matter more than any figure. First, registration under one regime is not registration under the other, and being outside one says nothing about the other; a business can be required to register for corporate tax while remaining below the VAT threshold, and the reverse. Second, the regime has thresholds that bear on whether tax is payable and at what level, and separate rules about who must register at all, so 'do we owe anything' and 'must we register' are two questions rather than one. The threshold figures, the registration criteria, the deadlines and the rates are published by the Federal Tax Authority and must be read there. The company's own position on corporate tax is a standing founder ruling recorded in public.company_registration and is read from that row before this subject is discussed at all.

structured_data.separate_from_vat: different registration, returns and thresholds; neither implies the other
structured_data.company_position: a standing founder ruling in public.company_registration.corporate_tax_note; read it first

title: Taxable income starts from accounting profit and is then adjusted
content: Corporate tax regimes generally do not compute their own profit from scratch. They take the profit shown in financial statements prepared under an accepted accounting framework and adjust it for items the law treats differently: costs that are not deductible, income that is exempt, timing differences where the law recognises something in a different period from the accounts, and relief provisions. The practical consequence for the bookkeeping is direct and worth stating plainly: the quality of the accounting records determines the reliability of the tax computation, so records kept loosely on the assumption that the tax is small produce a computation nobody can defend regardless of how small the tax turns out to be. Which adjustments apply, which accounting framework is accepted, and what reliefs exist are set by the current law and must be resolved from the Federal Tax Authority.

structured_data.starting_point: accounting profit under an accepted framework
structured_data.consequence: record quality determines computation reliability regardless of the amount at stake

title: Small business relief exists as an election, and the founder has ruled it is not raised
content: Corporate tax regimes commonly provide a relief for smaller businesses, typically operating as an election that a qualifying business makes for a period, with conditions and consequences attached to making it. Its existence is recorded here so that the subject is not mistaken for an oversight, and nothing further about it is: the qualifying conditions, the periods it is available for, and what electing it costs or forfeits are set by the current law and must be resolved from the Federal Tax Authority. A standing founder ruling recorded in public.company_registration additionally instructs that the founder is not to be asked about corporate tax registration, the first tax period, or small business relief, and that a registration task is opened only when revenue approaches the threshold. The accountant seat honours that: it monitors the measure and does not raise the subject with the founder until the measure requires it.

structured_data.what_it_is: an election available to qualifying smaller businesses, with conditions and consequences
structured_data.standing_ruling: do not ask the founder about corporate tax registration, the first tax period, or small business relief; open a task when revenue approaches the threshold

title: Record retention: an obligation exists, and the period is not stated here
content: A UAE business is required to keep accounting records and supporting documents, and to be able to produce them to the relevant authority on request. The retention obligation is real and it attaches to the underlying evidence, not only to the summarised accounts: invoices issued and received, bank and payment-processor records, contracts, and the working papers behind any figure filed with an authority. The number of years for which records must be kept is set in law, differs between regimes and for certain classes of record, and has been amended; for those reasons it is not stated in this record. It must be resolved from the current applicable authority before any retention or deletion policy is written, and a deletion schedule built on an assumed period is a compliance failure waiting for the first request that arrives after the documents were destroyed. Until the period is resolved, the safe operating rule is to retain.

structured_data.obligation: keep accounting records and supporting documents and produce them on request
structured_data.not_stated_here: the number of years, which differs by regime and record class and has been amended

title: Penalties exist and no penalty amount is recorded here
content: Tax regimes attach administrative penalties to failures such as registering late, filing late, paying late, and keeping inadequate records, and those penalties are frequently structured rather than flat, with fixed components, escalating components for repetition, and components computed on the amount and the delay. None of that structure and none of the amounts are recorded here, for the ordinary reason that penalty schedules are amended and a stale figure would be quoted with confidence. What is recorded is the operational consequence: because penalties commonly attach to lateness independently of whether tax was owed, a business that believes it owes nothing can still incur them by not filing, so the obligation to file and the obligation to pay are tracked as two separate things. Any actual penalty exposure must be resolved from the Federal Tax Authority's current publication for the specific failure and period concerned.

structure_commonly_includes: components computed on amount and delay
structured_data.operational_consequence: track the obligation to file separately from the obligation to pay

title: Obligations beyond tax that a UAE company may be subject to
content: Tax is not the whole of a company's regulatory surface. Depending on activity, ownership and structure, a UAE business may fall within economic substance requirements, ultimate beneficial ownership registration, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing obligations including registration on the relevant goAML platform for designated activities, data protection obligations, and sector-specific licensing conditions attached to the activities on its own trade licence. Whether any of these applies is a determination made against the current rules and the company's actual activities, not something assumed from its size, and several of them attach to the activity rather than to revenue, so a business with no income can still be in scope. This record exists so that the surface is known to exist and assessed deliberately; each obligation's applicability, content and any associated deadline must be resolved from the authority that administers it.

possible_obligations: AML and CFT obligations including goAML registration for designated activities
structured_data.determined_by: activity, ownership and structure against the current rules
structured_data.note: several attach to activity rather than revenue, so low income does not imply out of scope

title: Mainland and free zone are different positions, and the licence is what settles which
content: A UAE business is licensed either on the mainland by an emirate-level authority or within one of the free zones, and the two positions differ in ownership rules, in where and to whom the business may trade directly, and in how certain tax provisions apply. The determination is not a matter of interpretation: the licence itself names the authority that issued it, and the company's licence details are recorded in public.company_registration, which is what the accountant reads before answering any question that turns on this. What the licence also settles, and what is routinely overlooked, is which activities the business is permitted to carry on at all, listed by activity code on the licence itself; income from an activity the licence does not cover is a licensing problem before it is an accounting one. Any tax consequence attaching specifically to a free zone position must be resolved from the Federal Tax Authority and does not apply to a mainland licence.

two_positions: mainland, licensed by an emirate-level authority
structured_data.settled_by: the licence itself, recorded in public.company_registration
structured_data.also_settled_by_the_licence: the permitted activities, by activity code
structured_data.flag: income from an unlicensed activity is a licensing problem before it is an accounting one

title: Whether accounts must be audited is a determination, not a default
content: An audit is an independent examination of financial statements resulting in an opinion, and whether a given company is required to have one depends on its licensing authority, its structure and sometimes its size, not on a general expectation that companies are audited. The determination is made against the requirements of the authority that licensed the business and any others that apply to it. It is worth separating three things that get conflated: whether an audit is required, whether an auditor has been appointed, and whether the accounts are reliable. The third does not follow from the first two and is not delivered by them; it is delivered by the bookkeeping and the controls around it. The company's own recorded position on this is a standing founder ruling held in public.company_registration and is read from there rather than asked about.

structured_data.audit: an independent examination producing an opinion on financial statements
structured_data.required_or_not: determined by the licensing authority, structure and sometimes size
